title: Delegated canary guardrails and escalation playflow prototype
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Large product teams need fine-grained delegation for rollout safety. Currently the Redwood Console requires a single engineer to own canary configuration and emergency rollback. This creates delays and context loss during incidents and prevents operators from applying team-level guardrails.

Goal: Design a console flow that lets platform owners define delegated guardrails (e.g., maximum traffic ramp, automated health thresholds, escalation contacts), and allows on-call engineers to execute and escalate a canary with minimal friction. Deliver a clickable prototype for usability testing and a concise spec for engineering implementation.

Scope & deliverables:
- A new 'Delegation' panel under Rollouts where owners define role-scoped constraints and pre-approved rollback policies.
- A streamlined 'Quick Escalate' path in the live canary view: suggest actions based on signals, allow one-click rollback, and optionally trigger pre-defined playbooks.
- Visual timeline that shows who approved each guardrail change and the escalation chain if thresholds are breached.
- Accessibility and mobile-responsive considerations for on-call workflows.

Out of scope: Deep RBAC implementation (ENG will own), backend alerting plumbing, and audit-log storage mechanism (coord with ENG/PM).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype includes Delegation panel with editable guardrail presets and an approval history lane.
Live canary view prototype shows suggested remediation actions derived from guardrails and allows one-click rollback with confirmation flow.
Escalation playflow displays contact chain and an optional message template that can be triggered from the UI.
Design spec includes annotations for API inputs: guardrail JSON shape, allowed override roles, and required audit events (high-level).
Usability test plan with 6 participants and success metrics (time-to-rollback < 90s for approved users).
comments: 2025-03-06 — Asha Patel: Initial sketched flows completed. Added escalation chain UX and two guardrail presets (safe, aggressive). Leaving notes for ENG on API constraints.

2025-03-12 — Kofi Mensah (Eng Lead): Technical note — backend will provide 'delegationProfiles' API and 'escalationRunbookId'; we need to surface runbook selection in the UI. Also requested wireframes for mobile compact view.

2025-03-14 — Design critique (internal): Feedback to reduce cognitive load in the Delegation panel by collapsing advanced options and surfacing 'Preview effective policy' before save. Action: implement preview and microcopy updates.
2025-03-16 — Marco Chen: Updated prototype with preview and emergency bypass modal. Running quick internal test; prototype passes keyboard-only navigation checks. Preparing handoff doc for ENG.
2025-03-18 — Asha Patel: Submitted design spec to Confluence and linked PR for initial API contract. Seeking PM sign-off and scheduling usability sessions (Mar 20-21).
decisions: Default guardrail presets (Safe, Balanced, Aggressive) will be offered to reduce friction; teams can create custom profiles.
Emergency bypass is allowed only for users with 'Canary Operator' role; bypass action records a mandatory justification and triggers an immediate audit event.
Preview effective policy feature included to surface combined org + team + override rule set before applying changes.
One-click rollback will open a lightweight confirmation modal that shows predicted impact and required audit log entry; no rollback automatic retries from UI (engineers must re-trigger).
